product_change: Five-step frontend walkthrough across company knowledge, graph inspection, investigator handoff, fresh resolver and incident-specific memory

coverage: Starting the guide does not submit an action
Existing history cannot complete a newly started guide
Complete question-to-memory interaction sends explicit API commands
Directed graph records are required for the dependency path
Separate sessions, measured health and ticket closure are required for recovery completion
Only this incident's three memory kinds satisfy its memory step
Company answers exclude incident resolver summaries
Source inspection uses the captured revision
Escape closes the inspector and restores focus
A delayed source read cannot reopen a closed inspector
Leaving the guide does not cancel a running server job
An unfinished checkout links to its existing incident
No-match memory filters have an explanation and can be cleared
An interruption after recovery still offers resume to finish ticket closure

live_api_and_frontend_progress.method: Actual app API responses are passed to the same TypeScript evidence function used by the frontend; this is not browser interaction

initial_check_failures_retained: Three new DOM checks initially failed because the HTTP stub treated GET requests with an options object as mutations. Dispatch and assertions were corrected to inspect the POST method.
The initial Vitest include pattern excluded pure .test.ts files. It now includes both .test.ts and .test.tsx, so the six progress-rule checks execute.
browser_review_blocker: Computer-use native pipe unavailable; browser/app inventory empty
current_app_state: Original app running and idle; gateway, orders and payments HTTP 200
limits: Finite synthetic checks. DOM and live API checks do not establish desktop/mobile visual quality. Known citation locations do not verify claim entailment. Guide state resets on reload; backend work remains saved.
